t: You're at The Aldgate School, a Church of England primary school, and the only state-funded school in the City of London. It was founded in 1709 in the churchyard of St Botolph's Aldgate, and its last Ofsted report, in 2013, rated it Outstanding. The school's name was linked to Sir John Cass, who lived from 1666 to 1718. He was a merchant, Tory Member of Parliament and philanthropist, and also a key figure in the Royal African Company, which was involved in the Atlantic slave trade.
